question: What claim should OpenClaw support and which outbound paths may emit it: service-credential possession, a locally generated installation identity, or centrally or hardware-attested runtime identity?
rationale: These choices provide materially different guarantees, privacy properties, key-distribution requirements, and core-versus-plugin boundaries; implementation cannot safely choose among them.

options.title: Service-specific credential proof
options.body: Let each service or plugin issue audience-bound credentials and signed requests, without claiming that credential possession proves the absence of human control.

options.title: Local installation identity
options.body: Add an opt-in locally generated key and domain allowlist, explicitly documenting that it identifies a key-holding installation rather than an autonomous agent.

options.title: Central or hardware attestation
options.body: Defer implementation until OpenClaw has an authority, provisioning, revocation, hardware-root, replay, and privacy model capable of supporting the stronger claim.

recommendation.title: Service-specific credential proof
recommendation.body: Let each service or plugin issue audience-bound credentials and signed requests, without claiming that credential possession proves the absence of human control.
